explanations: terra: God raises the mountain above the covenant recipients and commands them to hold firmly and remember what it contains, joining elevation, a threatening overhead weight, and dhikr.

luna: A group given the Book casts it behind its backs as if they did not know; this repeated Qur’anic scene sharpens the section’s reversal from burdened or forgetful back to an elevated, remembered name. | terra: A group نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ ... كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ, repeating the section’s image of a remembered book displaced behind the back.

luna: Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House while praying for acceptance; the source-section root r-f-ʿ links this literal construction and elevation to the section’s raising of remembrance. | terra: إِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ ٱلْقَوَاعِدَ makes raising a construction act and immediately turns the builders to their Lord in a prayer for acceptance.

luna: The ayah asks who would turn away “عن ملة إبراهيم”; the source-section root r-gh-b names desire toward the Lord, so this opposed preposition and direction make a direct boundary around the section’s final “إلى ربك فارغب.” | terra: Who turns away from Abraham’s way except one who belittles himself? The root رغ ب appears with “away from,” clarifying how its preposition determines desire’s direction.

luna: 2:130 asks who turns away from Abraham’s way, and this next ayah answers with Abraham’s “أسلمت لرب العالمين”; its own contribution is an explicit submission to the Lord that completes the opposite direction to turning away.

luna: “اذكروني أذكركم” gives reciprocal remembrance between people and God; it adds a direct relationship to the section’s image of a name raised and held in remembrance. | terra: “Remember Me; I will remember you, and thank Me” turns divine favor into reciprocal remembrance and gratitude toward the benefactor.

luna: In the fasting rule, God intends ease and does not intend hardship; this concrete rule parallels the section’s law of ease amid difficulty and states the same ease-versus-hardship boundary in another setting. | terra: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ states ease and hardship as opposed divine intentions, illuminating surah 94’s more intimate coexistence “with.”

luna: After completing the rites, people are commanded to remember God; this is a direct finish-then-remembrance sequence corresponding to the section’s transition from completing work to rising for another directed act. | terra: فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُم مَّنَٰسِكَكُمْ فَٱذْكُرُوا ٱللَّهَ commands remembrance once rites are completed, a close procedural parallel to “when you are free, exert yourself.”

luna: After 2:200’s post-rites remembrance, this ayah records the prayer “ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة”; its own contribution is a desire directed to the Lord that includes both worldly and lasting good.
luna: Following the two prayers in 2:201, this ayah says each has a share of what they earned; it completes the link between directed desire and the worker’s eventual portion.
terra: Believers are touched by suffering and shaken until the messenger asks when help will come; “God’s help is near” places relief within the hardship scene.

luna: This nursing passage forbids harming a mother or father because of the child and requires consultation about weaning; it gives the specific parent-and-nursing burden that the section places beside childbirth. | terra: The nursing settlement says لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا and forbids either parent being harmed through the child, defining ease within the weight of care.

luna: The command to stand before God devoutly gives a direct posture of standing in worship, a possible specific counterpart to the section’s word nasb as raising oneself upright. | terra: The command to preserve the prayers ends with standing devoutly before God, a direct bodily counterpart to rising for Lord-directed work.
terra: A “good loan” is followed by وَٱللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْصُطُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ, joining debt, constriction/expansion, and return to God.
terra: The Ark contains سَكِينَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ and is تَحْمِلُهُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ, joining a carried container with Lord-given tranquility rather than oppressive cargo.
terra: رَبَّنَآ أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا pictures patience poured from a vessel and immediately asks for firm feet, joining emptying with steadfast posture toward God.
terra: وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَٰتٍ places differing elevated ranks among messengers, the prophetic-status dimension of the raised mention.

luna: The debtor in hardship must be given respite until ease, and remission is praised; this is the section’s debt scene, where the due weight is allowed to remain until the debtor can bear it. | terra: وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيْسَرَةٍ makes debt a carried constriction and commands respite until spacious ease arrives.
terra: Immediately after the distressed debtor and remission in 2:280, this ayah says تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ and every soul is paid in full.

luna: The closing prayer asks God not to lay on people a burden like the one laid on those before and asks for pardon and mercy; it gives a direct supplication for the load the section says God removes. | terra: The prayer لَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَآ إِصْرًا ... وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ asks the Lord not to impose a back-breaking burden.
terra: Love of worldly desires and possessions is set against the good return with God, giving the section’s directed رغبة a concrete rival inventory.
terra: Mary’s mother says إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ; وَضَعَ here is exactly the childbirth sense of “put down” developed from the section’s unloading verb.

luna: A group receives the Scripture and then casts it behind their backs; the section explicitly recalls this scene as the opposite of a name raised above the back and kept in memory. | terra: Those charged to make scripture known نَبَذُوهُ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ; revelation is forgotten behind the back rather than its remembrance being raised and heard.

luna: The believers remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides, then reflect on creation and pray; this directly joins upright posture and remembrance in a devotional stance. | terra: Those who remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides join dhikr to the back’s changing bodily postures without letting posture interrupt remembrance.

luna: The ayah says God wishes to lighten for people because the human was created weak; that is a specific divine easing of human constraint, supporting the section’s broadening of relief beyond one personal load. | terra: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ grounds divine lightening in human weakness, a general statement of the load-removing act pictured in the section.

luna: After prayer, believers are commanded to remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides; this connects the section’s upright posture and continued remembrance to a concrete worship sequence after an activity. | terra: فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱذْكُرُوا ٱللَّهَ standing, sitting, and reclining makes completion immediately open into another intentional act of remembrance.

luna: After setting out ablution and purification, this ayah says God does not intend difficulty but intends purification and completion of favor; it ties relief from difficulty to a divine gift as the section does. | terra: مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ presents ritual commands as purification rather than constriction, supporting the section’s distinction between burden and directed work.
terra: The command to race in good works is framed by the return of everyone to God, joining strenuous action to its Lordward endpoint.
terra: “Rather, His hands are outspread; He spends as He wills” uses spreading for unrestricted divine giving, a provision sense beside the section’s garment and chest expansion.
terra: Erected cult stones are named among defilements to avoid, setting a worship boundary around the root whose physical sense is “set upright.”

luna: The people who deny the meeting are described as carrying “أوزارهم على ظهورهم”; the source-section root w-z-r and its load-on-the-back image become an explicit scene of burdens carried on backs. | terra: وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ أَوْزَارَهُمْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِمْ explicitly places awzār on backs, the literalized moral load from which the section’s addressee is released.
terra: In the darkness of land and sea people call humbly and promise gratitude if rescued; 6:64 tests that promised turn after the burden is removed.
terra: God rescues from that distress and every anguish, “then you associate,” reversing the relieved bearer’s faithful return to the benefactor.

luna: God expands the breast of one He guides toward Islam and makes another’s breast constricted; the source-section root sh-r-ḥ is therefore given a clear direction and boundary, expansion toward guidance rather than any destination. | terra: God يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُۥ لِلْإِسْلَامِ, while the contrary breast is ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا as though climbing upward; it gives both expansion and its bodily reversal.
terra: Cattle are divided into burden-bearers and smaller stock, then people are told to eat God’s provision, linking animal loads to provision from the giver.
luna: In commands about an orphan’s property, fair measure, and just speech, God says no soul is burdened beyond its capacity; it applies the burden limit to concrete obligations.
luna: The Prophet declares that his prayer, rites, life, and death are for God; this is a concrete statement of the whole worker’s direction toward the Lord in the section’s final movement.

luna: After 6:162 dedicates prayer, rites, life, and death to God, this ayah says He has no partner and that the speaker is commanded to be among the Muslims; it completes the declaration of directed devotion.

luna: The ayah says no bearer bears another’s burden while stressing that each person earns against himself; this is a repeated boundary on human load-sharing that clarifies the section’s divine removal of the load. | terra: وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ limits the minister image: moral burden cannot simply be transferred, and the ayah ends with return to your Lord.
terra: فَلَا يَكُن فِى صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُۥ denies constriction in the messenger’s breast so that he can warn with the revealed book.
luna: The believers who do good are described as not being burdened beyond their capacity and as people of the Garden; this is another direct limit on the load a person is assigned.
terra: The threatened magicians answer إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ; 7:126 then turns that declared return into a prayer for poured patience.
terra: رَبَّنَآ أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا asks the Lord to pour patience upon threatened believers and let them die submitted, combining vessel imagery with unwavering direction.

luna: In describing the Messenger’s followers, this ayah says he removes “إصرهم والأغلال” from them; that unloading of burden and shackles parallels the section’s load taken off the back and makes relief concrete. | terra: وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَٱلْأَغْلَٰلَ reproduces the section’s decisive action: a divinely sent messenger puts down the burden and restraints carried by people.
terra: The mountain is lifted over the people like a canopy, and they are commanded to hold the gift firmly and remember it; raised structure and retained remembrance meet again.
terra: Pregnancy passes from حَمْلًا خَفِيفًا to فَلَمَّآ أَثْقَلَت, whereupon the parents call their Lord; bodily heaviness itself turns the bearers toward the benefactor.
terra: After the heavy pregnancy’s prayer and a sound child, جَعَلَا لَهُۥ شُرَكَآءَ; it reverses grateful Lordward movement after a load is safely delivered.
luna: The command to remember the Lord inwardly and “دون الجهر من القول” (without loud speech) engages the source-section’s dictionary sense of dhikr as sound while specifying a quieter mode.

luna: The believers’ hearts tremble when God is mentioned, their faith increases when His verses are recited, and they trust their Lord; this gives another specific meeting of remembrance, inward response, and reliance on God.
terra: After saying God and His Messenger sufficed them, the speakers say إِنَّآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ رَٰغِبُونَ; received provision becomes desire directed back to its giver.
terra: A building founded on an undermined cliff collapses with its builder into fire, opposing the stable construction and upright posture developed in the section.
terra: God turns mercifully toward the Prophet and followers who accompanied him in the hour of hardship after some hearts nearly swerved, joining strain with sustaining return.
terra: The three find أَن لَّا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيْهِ; constriction gives way to the discovery that refuge from God lies only in turning to Him.
terra: No thirst, نَصَبٌ, or hunger suffered فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ goes unrecorded; this is explicitly Lord-directed fatigue rather than fatigue from a back’s load.

luna: When harm touches a person, he calls on God lying, sitting, or standing; once God removes it, he passes as if he had never called. The reversal directly contrasts with the section’s person who rises and turns to God after relief. | terra: After God removes human harm مَرَّ كَأَن لَّمْ يَدْعُنَآ, reversing the section’s relieved person who rises and turns deliberately to the benefactor.

luna: People aboard ships call to God sincerely when a storm strikes, promise gratitude if saved, then commit wrong after rescue; this is a sea-and-relief reversal of the section’s response of turning to the Lord after help. | terra: A storm at sea makes travelers call God sincerely and promise gratitude upon rescue; their intended direction is reversed in 10:23.
terra: As soon as God rescues them, the travelers transgress on earth, reversing the remembered favor and Lordward return of the mounted traveler.
terra: The Quran is مَوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَشِفَآءٌ لِّمَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ, giving a Lord-sent inward remedy corresponding to an opened, tranquil breast.
terra: وَضَآئِقٌۢ بِهِۦ صَدْرُكَ addresses the Prophet’s breast constricted by demands placed on his proclamation, the experienced reverse of divinely opened space.
terra: Accounts of earlier messengers are narrated to steady the Prophet’s heart, another direct image of divine support given inside the breast for its task.
terra: Joseph asks a companion to mention him to his master, but that mention is forgotten; dhikr here moves between voiced name and failed memory.
terra: God knows what every female bears, what wombs diminish or increase, and everything with Him has a measure; pregnancy-load and exact fitting are joined.
terra: ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ makes provision itself spacious or constrained and adds the risk of rejoicing in nearer life.

luna: This ayah says hearts find tranquility in remembrance of God; it links the section’s opened, settled chest to dhikr, adding an explicit account of how remembrance calms the heart. | terra: أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ joins remembrance to settled hearts, supplying the inner repose of the section’s widened breast.
terra: Those who prefer worldly life to the Hereafter also turn others from God’s way, making wrongly directed preference deform the path of action.
terra: لَا يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيهَا نَصَبٌ likewise removes all weariness from the garden, distinguishing enduring rest from present exertion.
terra: وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ names the same addressee’s constricted breast; 15:98–99 answer it with Lord-directed worship.
terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ turns the constricted breast of 15:97 into commanded bodily worship toward the Lord.
terra: وَٱعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَكَ ٱلْيَقِينُ makes the response to chest-constriction sustained labor for the Lord.

luna: God’s animals carry heavy loads to distant lands that people could not reach without hardship; this supplies a literal burden-bearing transport scene alongside the section’s back and mount imagery. | terra: Cattle تَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ to a distant land reachable only بِشِقِّ ٱلْأَنفُسِ, making the caravan back, load, road, and hardship one literal scene.

luna: 16:7 describes animals carrying heavy loads, and this next ayah names horses, mules, and donkeys for riding and adornment; its own contribution is the range of mounts behind the section’s riding image. | terra: Horses, mules, and donkeys are created to be ridden, continuing 16:7’s burden-bearing caravan with the rider’s upright use of the animal.

luna: Those who mislead are said to bear their own full burdens and burdens along with their own; this is a further contrary case of burdens added through one’s actions. | terra: Misleaders يَحْمِلُوا۟ أَوْزَارَهُمْ ... وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُم; their added burdens arise from causing others’ error, not innocent transfer.
terra: God attacks a building from its foundations so the roof falls on its makers, the structural reversal of a load removed so that a person can stand.
terra: Every blessing is from God, and under harm فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْـَٔرُونَ; 16:54 tests whether that directed cry survives after relief.
terra: After God removes the harm, a group يُشْرِكُونَ بِرَبِّهِمْ; release from weight leads away from the Lord instead of back to Him.
terra: God brings people from their mothers’ wombs, gives hearing, sight, and hearts, and states gratitude as the intended response to that deliverance.

luna: The passage contrasts a heart secure in faith with those who “شرحوا بالكفر صدرا”; the source-section root sh-r-ḥ thus also names a breast opened toward disbelief, the contrary direction to its final desire for God. | terra: مَّن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا shows that opening a breast is directionally neutral as an image; here its content is unbelief, opposite the section’s Lordward end.
terra: A secure town receiving abundant provision denies God’s favors and is made to taste a garment of hunger and fear, reversing breadth into enveloping constriction.
terra: Eat the lawful provision God gave and thank His favor if Him you worship; provision becomes the ground for directed human response.

luna: In the passage about guidance and each person’s own account, it says no bearer of burden bears another’s burden; this reiterates the limit on transferring a load to a helper. | terra: The repeated وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ marks personal responsibility, distinguishing divine removal of a burden from another person carrying it.

luna: This ayah describes one who desires the immediate life and is given some of it; it concretely supplies the worldly direction the section says an opened chest could take. | terra: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ receives only the hastened worldly allotment; 17:19 reverses both the object of desire and the quality of striving.

luna: By contrast with 17:18, this ayah describes one who desires the Hereafter and strives for it as a believer; that specific desire-plus-effort pattern matches the section’s command to work and direct longing to God. | terra: Whoever desires the Hereafter وَسَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا has their striving appreciated; desire and labor receive value from their chosen direction.
terra: The hand must be neither chained to the neck nor fully outspread; spending is pictured through bodily constriction and expansion that both require measure.
terra: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ supplies the economic expansion and narrowing behind the section’s “provision constrained” scene.

luna: At sea, people call only upon God in distress, then turn away when He saves them to land; this directly reverses the section’s Godward return after removal of a burden and also continues the mount-and-travel scene. | terra: When God rescues distressed sailors to land أَعْرَضْتُمْ, a sharp maritime reversal of the rider who remembers favor and returns toward the Lord.
terra: The addressee is commanded to rise for extra night worship so that his Lord may raise him مَقَامًا مَّحْمُودًا; exertion and elevated prophetic station are causally joined.
luna: When God bestows favor on a person, he turns away and withdraws; this states the opposite of the section’s person whose removed burden leads him back to his benefactor.
terra: God binds the youths’ hearts when they stand and declare “Our Lord,” joining an inwardly strengthened vessel, upright posture, voiced witness, and Lordward direction.
terra: “Remember your Lord when you forget” directly turns a lapse of memory into renewed Lordward attention.
terra: The addressee is told he will find no مُلْتَحَدًا apart from God after reciting revelation, another refuge-word supporting the section’s semantic link from wazar to Lord.
terra: Remain with those who call their Lord يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ and do not look past them toward worldly adornment; it fixes desire’s direction against the worldly alternative.
terra: One reminded of the Lord’s signs turns away and forgets what his hands sent ahead; reminder is displaced into deliberate forgetting rather than raised and retained.
terra: Those awaiting the appointed time will find no place of escape apart from it, a semantic parallel to the section’s “no wazar” refuge boundary.

luna: After Moses and his companion continue their journey to meet the servant they seek, Moses says they have met “نصبا,” fatigue; this shares the source-section root n-ṣ-b and its purposeful labor, while its context makes the exertion a journey of seeking. | terra: لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًا makes nasb the fatigue of Moses’ journey, close to the road-weariness distinguished from a burdened back.
terra: Moses asks لَا تُرْهِقْنِى مِنْ أَمْرِى عُسْرًا; difficulty in an affair is described as something laid heavily upon him.
terra: The wall يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُ meets both sides of the section’s posture: a structure about to collapse is made upright.
terra: أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا is a literal command to pour molten copper over the newly erected barrier, preserving the bucket-emptying sense beside purposeful work.
terra: Mary carries the child and withdraws to a distant place; this ayah contributes the pregnancy-load whose labor and relief unfold in 19:23–26.

luna: Mary’s labor drives her to the trunk of a palm tree and she voices anguish; this supplies a vivid birth scene of bodily strain corresponding to the section’s childbirth image. | terra: Labor drives Mary to the palm trunk and makes her voice extremity; this is the birth scene’s bodily hardship before the easing provisions in the following ayat.

luna: After Mary’s anguish in 19:23, a caller tells her not to grieve and points to a stream made by her Lord; this ayah contributes immediate divine provision within the birth scene. | terra: A voice tells Mary not to grieve because her Lord has placed a stream below her, supplying immediate Lord-given relief within the labor scene.

luna: After the stream is announced, Mary is told to shake the palm trunk so fresh dates will fall; this ayah adds food and a concrete means of relief during the difficult birth. | terra: Mary must shake the palm trunk so ripe dates fall; relief includes newly commanded exertion by the recipient rather than passive release alone.

luna: After the water and dates in 19:24–25, Mary is told to eat, drink, and be comforted; this ayah completes the sequence of provision and ease around the birth. | terra: “Eat, drink, and be comforted” completes the birth passage with bodily ease and then gives Mary a new deliberate course of action.
luna: The command to mention Abraham in the Book introduces his account; this is another concrete formulation of a person’s name being kept in remembrance.
terra: Abraham’s father asks whether he is turning away from his gods; the same راغب construction points away from a false object and implicitly toward the true Lord.

luna: God grants Abraham’s descendants mercy and “لسان صدق عليا,” a high, truthful renown; this is a concrete instance of the source-section’s remembrance as honor raised to a high place. | terra: وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا combines lasting renown with height, closely matching the section’s status, voice, and memory senses of elevated dhikr.
terra: وَرَفَعْنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا makes raising a person mean elevated station, clarifying the rank sense within “raising” the addressee’s mention.
terra: The heavens nearly rupture, earth splits, and mountains collapse at the claim attributed to God; a spoken theological weight is rendered as structural cracking.
terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ joins divinely made ease to the addressee’s tongue so that proclamation can warn and give good news.
terra: مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰ denies that revelation was sent to make the prophetic addressee wretched; 20:3 identifies it instead as remembrance.
terra: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ completes 20:2’s removal of distress with remembrance, matching the section’s descent of burden and ascent of dhikr.

luna: Before Moses asks for an opened chest, ease, and a helper, God commands him to go to Pharaoh, who has transgressed; this ayah supplies the mission that makes the later requests for capacity and support intelligible.

luna: Moses begins by asking “اشرح لي صدري”; the source-section root sh-r-ḥ links this opening of the chest to the section’s first expansion, while his petition makes the receiving of expanded capacity explicit. | terra: Moses’ prayer رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى is the section’s explicit parallel for a breast expanded before the burdened task is addressed.

luna: Moses immediately asks “ويسر لي أمري” after the chest-opening request; the sequence joins expanded capacity to an eased task, a pairing the section develops before the burden is lifted. | terra: Moses next asks وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى; this ayah supplies the ease immediately following the opened breast of 20:25.
terra: وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى places released speech between opened breast/eased task and requested minister, anticipating the section’s sound sense of dhikr.
terra: يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى gives the purpose of Moses’ released tongue: words must become heard and retained by others, complementing elevated remembrance.

luna: Moses asks for a “وزير” from his family; the source-section root w-z-r names the bearer behind 94’s word for burden, so this passage stages the helper that the section says its own speaker does not need. | terra: Moses asks وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِى, naming the burden-sharing minister whom the section contrasts with the direct removal of the Prophet’s wizr.

luna: 20:29 requests a family vizier, and this next ayah names Harun as that helper; the name completes the human-support scene that contrasts with the burden removed directly in the section. | terra: هَٰرُونَ أَخِى identifies the family member asked for as minister and prepares the strengthening function stated in 20:31.

luna: After 20:30 names Aaron, Moses asks that his back be strengthened through him; this is an especially close back-and-helper image beside the section’s burdened back and its contrast with Moses’ requested vizier. | terra: Moses asks ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى; Aaron’s role is to strengthen the support that bears the task, making the section’s minister/back connection concrete.

luna: Moses asks for Aaron to share his task; this ayah contributes the shared-work aspect of the helper requested in the preceding verses, in contrast to the section’s burden being removed directly. | terra: وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى states what the minister is for: sharing Moses’ affair, unlike the solitary addressee whose burden God removes in surah 94.
luna: Moses says that he and Aaron may glorify God much; this next step connects the requested help to worship, clarifying the aim of the work.
luna: Moses adds that they may remember God much; this completes the helper prayer with the same remembrance theme that follows the section’s raised name.
terra: قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ confirms that the linked requests for expanded breast, ease, and a supporting minister were divinely granted.
terra: حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا stages material loads being carried and then cast down, though their unloading leads into the calf episode.

luna: The one who turns away from God’s remembrance bears a burden on Resurrection Day; it is the section’s exact reverse, where turning from dhikr is joined to load-bearing rather than load-removal and elevated mention. | terra: Whoever turns from ذِكْرِى يَحْمِلْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وِزْرًا; remembrance refused becomes the very burden the section opposes to elevated remembrance.
terra: وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ حِمْلًا names the enduring load’s bad weight and completes the burden introduced in 20:100.
terra: Whoever turns from My remembrance receives a constricted life; the ayah directly reverses the section’s pairing of raised remembrance with opened space.

luna: The people are told that a Book has come containing “ذكركم”; the source-section root dh-k-r includes honor and mention, and this ayah makes remembrance a defining address to a whole people. | terra: A revealed book فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ can mean both reminder and the hearers’ honor, echoing the section’s deliberate preservation of dhikr’s several senses.

luna: The prophets are described as hastening in good deeds and calling upon God “رغبا ورهبا”; this uses the source-section root r-gh-b for desire in a specifically God-directed supplication. | terra: وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا describes prophets calling God in desire and fear, giving the section’s directed رغبة a worshipful stance.
terra: The Hour makes كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا lay down her pregnancy in terror; it is childbirth-as-unloading under catastrophe rather than merciful ease.
terra: Pilgrims come on foot and on lean camels from every distant road in answer to the call, turning arduous caravan travel into movement toward worship.
terra: Sacrificial camels stand in rows while God’s name is pronounced; after they fall, their benefits are shared, and their subjection is tied to gratitude.
terra: Neither flesh nor blood reaches God, but reverence does; the animals were subjected so recipients might magnify God for His guidance.

luna: The ayah says God has placed no hardship in the religion, in a passage commanding striving for Him; this is a specific boundary on religious effort that complements the section’s ease amid hardship. | terra: The command to strive for God is paired with وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ, combining Lordward exertion with the denial of constricting burden.
luna: The ayah points to livestock as a lesson, with drink and benefits from them; it supplies another specific Qur’anic context for the animal provision that underlies riding and carrying.
luna: After 23:21 describes livestock’s benefits, this ayah says people are carried on them and on ships; its own contribution is the explicit riding-and-transport scene.
luna: God says no soul is burdened beyond its capacity and that a truthful record is with Him; this states a direct limit on burden-bearing and adds an account of what each person does.

luna: God permits houses “أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه”; this ayah directly joins raising a structure to remembrance of His name, meeting the section’s linked ideas of building, elevation, and a name kept present. | terra: Houses God permits أَن تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُ join raising, voiced remembrance, and a name in one construction.

luna: The next ayah says commerce and sale do not distract these people from remembering God and establishing prayer; it contributes workers who keep their direction through worldly tasks, the section’s final labor-and-desire scene. | terra: People whom trade does not distract عَن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ enact the section’s worker whose occupations remain ordered toward remembrance; 24:36 supplies raised houses and the voiced name.
terra: The Quran is disclosed gradually in order to strengthen the Prophet’s heart, showing revelation making the inward bearer fit for a weighty word.
terra: God says He made Aaron a وَزِيرًا with Moses; this is the other explicit Quranic naming of the helper through the word the section links to burden-bearing.
terra: Those who spend the night لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَٰمًا embody bodily, Lord-directed exertion, including the upright stance implied by fanṣab.
luna: In another account of Moses’ mission to Pharaoh, Moses voices fear that the people will deny him; this supplies the pressure surrounding his request for aid in the next ayat.

luna: Moses says his chest tightens and his tongue is not free, and asks that Aaron be sent; this is a direct contrary chest scene to the source-section root sh-r-ḥ and its opened chest before a task. | terra: Moses says وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ; constricted breast, blocked voice, and Aaron’s help converge.
luna: Moses says he fears they may kill him; this completes the concrete danger behind the narrowed-chest and helper request in 26:12–13.
luna: God tells Moses and Aaron to go with the signs and says He is with them, hearing; this contributes divine assurance and support after the constriction and fear Moses voiced.
luna: The next ayah commands Moses and Aaron to go to Pharaoh and state that they are messengers of the Lord of the worlds; it completes the task for which the chest and helper were needed.
terra: The magicians again say إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ while facing punishment, making Lordward return the direction that holds through imposed hardship.

luna: Abraham asks God to make for him a truthful mention among later generations; the prayer gives a direct counterpart to the section’s claim that God raises the addressee’s remembrance. | terra: Abraham asks وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ, a “truthful tongue” among later peoples that states the remembered, audible name image without رَفَعَ.

luna: The source-section root f-r-gh in “فرغت إلى” is glossed as deliberately turning to an undertaking; 28:10 instead says Moses’ mother’s heart became “فارغا” after she placed him in the river. The shared root and emptied-heart image are specific, though this is a different sense and a fearful scene rather than purposeful work. | terra: وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا makes the heart an emptied vessel, while God’s binding it shows emptiness made fit to hold a faithful purpose.
terra: Moses calls Aaron أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا and asks that he be sent as support, connecting the helper to audible speech as well as shared burden.

luna: God promises Moses that He will strengthen him through his brother and give them authority; this is another explicit divine provision of a human helper for the mission, beside the section’s burden removed without a vizier. | terra: God answers Moses, سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ; strengthening his arm through Aaron precisely stages a helper enabling the burdened speaker to stand and act.
terra: Qarun’s treasure-keys لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُوَّةِ make wealth a load that bends even a strong group; 28:82 reinterprets wealth as provision expanded or constrained by God.

luna: The command is to seek the Hereafter with what God has given while not forgetting one’s worldly share; this gives a specific balance between worldly provision and the ultimate direction toward God.
terra: Observers of Qarun confess ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ, turning the story of burdening wealth into recognition of its divine measure.
luna: The mother’s carrying and delivery “كرها” supply a second direct formulation of childbirth under strain, the birth-weight image that the section places beside debt and riding.

luna: Those who mislead are said to bear their own burdens and additional burdens; this is a contrary load-sharing case that clarifies the moral weight attached to the source-section’s root w-z-r. | terra: وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالًا مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ answers the false offer to carry others’ sins with accumulated loads of responsibility.
terra: Seek provision from God, worship Him, thank Him, and to Him you will return: received sustenance, active service, gratitude, and final direction occur in one command sequence.
terra: People cannot escape God in earth or heaven and have no protector or helper apart from Him, extending the no-refuge claim without using wazar.
terra: ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ repeats the section’s economic breadth and restriction as a divine act known by God.

luna: Those boarding a ship invoke God sincerely in danger, but associate others once safely on land; this gives a clear contrary response to the section’s final desire toward the benefactor after relief. | terra: Ship passengers call God with exclusive devotion, but once He saves them to land they associate partners, a complete relief-then-misdirection reversal.
luna: God promises to guide those who strive for Him to His ways and says He is with the doers of good; this directly links purposeful effort for God to guidance.

luna: When hardship touches people they call their Lord, but after He lets them taste mercy some associate others with Him; this is an explicit reversal of the section’s steady desire toward the Lord after help. | terra: People call their Lord مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ under harm, but after mercy a faction associates partners; the turn to the giver fails once the burden lifts.
terra: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ asks readers to see signs in provision’s expansion and constriction.

luna: The mother is said to have carried her child “وهنا على وهن”; this makes bodily carrying a child through successive weakness a direct counterpart to the section’s pregnancy-as-weight image. | terra: حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ وَهْنًا عَلَىٰ وَهْنٍ describes the mother’s weakening load and ends أَنِ ٱشْكُرْ لِى ... إِلَىَّ ٱلْمَصِيرُ, moving from carried weight to grateful return.

luna: People in shipboard waves call God sincerely, but after rescue some remain moderate and others reject; the ayah supplies a divided response after relief that sharpens the section’s chosen Godward turn.
terra: The question “Who can protect you from God?” denies any protector apart from Him whether He intends harm or mercy, reinforcing exclusive refuge and direction.

luna: God and His angels bless the Prophet and believers are commanded to bless and greet him; this is a concrete act of honoring the addressee, related to the section’s elevated remembrance. | terra: God and the angels bless the Prophet, then believers are commanded صَلُّوا۟ عَلَيْهِ; his mention is made public and continually voiced by divine act and human response.
terra: The heavens, earth, and mountains refuse أَن يَحْمِلْنَهَا, but the human حَمَلَهَا; the Trust supplies the cosmic boundary for what a bearer can take on.
terra: إِنَّ رَبِّى يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ corrects the belief that wealth proves rank, separating spacious provision from true elevation.
terra: إِنَّ رَبِّى يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ is followed by God replacing what people spend, linking economic breadth to active response.
terra: وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنثَىٰ وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ preserves both bearing and laying down a pregnancy under divine knowledge.

luna: A heavily burdened soul cannot have another carry its burden even if the other is a close relative; this gives a literalized boundary on human load-sharing beside the section’s burden removed by God. | terra: وَإِن تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌ makes the boundary bodily: even a near relation cannot shoulder the heavily laden person’s load.

luna: In the Garden of settlement, the people say no fatigue or weariness touches them; this provides a contrary boundary to the section’s tiring work here, with relief from exertion as an eventual state. | terra: لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ marks the final abode as free of fatigue, a boundary beyond the present Lord-directed work.
terra: God subdues cattle so that some become mounts and others food, presenting riding as a received divine act before 36:73 asks for gratitude.
terra: The mounted animals also give benefits and drink, then the ayah asks whether people will be grateful; conveyance should turn its beneficiary toward the giver.
luna: God says He left Noah’s mention among later generations; this is a concrete instance of remembrance preserved beyond the immediate scene, paralleling the raised name in the section.
luna: 37:78 preserves Noah’s mention among later generations, and this ayah adds “سلام على نوح في العالمين”; its own contribution is the honor attached to that enduring mention.
luna: God says He left Abraham’s mention among later generations; it repeats the concrete preservation of a person’s name that the section calls raised remembrance.
luna: 37:108 says Abraham’s mention remains among later generations, and this ayah adds “سلام على إبراهيم”; its own contribution is the honor that gives that enduring mention its tone.

luna: God says He left Moses and Aaron’s mention among later generations; this is another specific case of their remembrance being preserved beyond their own time. | terra: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِمَا فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ says Moses and Aaron are left in later memory; 37:120 voices that enduring mention.

luna: 37:119 preserves Moses and Aaron’s mention among later generations, and this ayah adds “سلام على موسى وهارون”; it contributes the honor joined to their lasting mention. | terra: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ is the actual sound preserved among later peoples, and it concerns the same prophet–minister pair developed in the section.
luna: God says He left Elias’s mention among later generations; this repeated formulation directly parallels the section’s image of a name raised and remembered.
luna: 37:129 preserves Elias’s mention among later generations, and this ayah adds “سلام على إل ياسين”; its own contribution is the honor attached to that lasting remembrance.
terra: Job’s أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ preserves nasb as afflicting exhaustion rather than the section’s commanded exertion.

luna: The ayah says no bearer bears another’s burden and that each person’s disbelief is against himself; this is another explicit boundary on who carries a load. | terra: No bearer bears another’s burden, then إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ; individual load and Lordward return meet as a limit on human burden-sharing.

luna: A person calls the Lord in hardship with turning devotion, then forgets Him when granted favor; this directly marks the failure that the section’s final turn after relief answers. | terra: A distressed person calls رَبَّهُۥ مُنِيبًا إِلَيْهِ, but after receiving favor نَسِىَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ; direction collapses into forgetting.

luna: This ayah joins a breast expanded by God to Islam with light from its Lord, then contrasts it with hearts hardened against God’s remembrance; it brings the section’s opening chest, divine light, and raised remembrance together. | terra: فَمَن شَرَحَ ٱللَّهُ صَدْرَهُۥ لِلْإِسْلَامِ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ directly joins God’s opening of the breast to the divine light in the section’s dictionary gloss.

luna: After 39:22 speaks of a breast expanded by God and hearts hardened against remembrance, this ayah describes the revealed best statement making skins shiver and then soften to God’s remembrance; it completes the bodily response to remembrance. | terra: The best discourse makes skins shiver and then skins and hearts soften to God’s remembrance, giving remembrance a bodily passage from tension into receptive ease.
terra: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ makes changing provision a sign rather than an autonomous measure of ease.
terra: God makes cattle so that people ride some and eat some; it introduces the mount whose relation to needs held in breasts is stated in 40:80.
terra: وَلِتَبْلُغُوا۟ عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِى صُدُورِكُمْ وَعَلَيْهَا ... تُحْمَلُونَ unusually joins a need held in breasts with being carried on animals.
terra: وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنثَىٰ وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ repeats pregnancy as a burden eventually put down, though ease is not stated here.

luna: The person who receives favor turns away and draws aside, while he prays at length when harm touches him; this is a second direct reversal of the section’s post-relief orientation. | terra: When favored, the human turns away and withdraws, but when harm touches him he makes lengthy supplication; ease and burden produce the opposite of stable direction.
terra: The heavens nearly split from above while angels glorify their Lord’s praise, placing a cracking structure beside voiced Lord-directed remembrance.
terra: لَهُۥ مَقَالِيدُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ places breadth and restriction under the Lord’s control.
terra: The harvest of the Hereafter is increased, while one who wants حَرْثَ ٱلدُّنْيَا receives some with no Hereafter share; work’s yield follows desire’s direction.
terra: Were God to بَسَطَ ٱلرِّزْقَ without measure, people would transgress; expansion itself needs a divinely fitted limit and is not unqualified ease.
terra: مَا لَكُم مِّن مَّلْجَإٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ repeats the no-refuge boundary and commands response to the Lord before that day.

luna: This ayah introduces ships and livestock as mounts; 43:13 completes the scene by settling on their backs and remembering God, while 43:14 gives the riders’ return to their Lord. This row supplies the rideable creatures. | terra: God makes ships and cattle for people to ride; this ayah supplies the conveyance whose backs, remembered favor, and Lordward return are stated in 43:13–14.

luna: The riders settle “على ظهورها” and then remember their Lord’s blessing; this is the section’s specific mount-back, back-to-remembrance sequence, with riding joined to gratitude. | terra: The rider settles عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِۦ and then remembers the Lord’s favor; back, upright settling, remembrance, and benefaction occur in the section’s order.

luna: The riding scene ends with “إلى ربنا لمنقلبون”; this ayah contributes the riders’ stated return to their Lord, which echoes the section’s final “إلى ربك.” | terra: The mounted traveler says وَإِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ, turning the ride on an animal’s back into movement toward the Lord.

luna: The Revelation is called a remembrance for the Prophet and his people, who will be questioned about it; this specific communal address relates to the section’s remembrance raised for its addressee. | terra: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ allows dhikr to mean the addressee’s honor or renown as well as reminder, the semantic meeting developed in the section.
terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ joins ease, the addressee’s audible tongue, and remembrance.
luna: The ayah describes one who takes his own desire as his god; this names a boundary opposite to the section’s desire deliberately directed toward the Lord.

luna: This ayah says a mother carried and gave birth to her child with hardship; its paired carrying and delivery stages correspond to the section’s birth scene and sharpen the weight’s release at birth. | terra: حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرْهًا وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًا gives the section’s dictionary movement literally: a child is borne as hardship and then laid down in birth.
terra: حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا brings the section’s two words together: war itself “puts down” its awzār, picturing hardship ending as an unloaded burden.

luna: God sends tranquility into the believers’ hearts; this gives a direct Qur’anic scene of inward calm bestowed by God, matching the source section’s gloss of opened breast as light and tranquility. | terra: هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ states the divine tranquility entering hearts that the section’s dictionary gloss uses to explain breast-opening.
luna: Believers are told to support and honor the Messenger and glorify God morning and evening; it supplies a concrete form of public honor alongside the section’s raised name.
terra: The shoot فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ ... فَٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ is strengthened by support until it stands on its stem, a living analogue of help restoring uprightness.
terra: لَا تَرْفَعُوا۟ أَصْوَٰتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِىِّ sets a boundary: God raises the Prophet’s heard mention, while believers may not raise their own voices over his.
terra: Those who يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَٰتَهُمْ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ enact the human lowering of voice that complements the boundary in 49:2.
terra: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا بِأَيْي۟دٍ presents divine building and expansive power; 51:48 turns to the earth made spread beneath it.
terra: وَٱلْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَٰهَا pictures the earth spread like furnishing, a cosmic counterpart to the section’s garment and opened-space imagery.
luna: The command “ففروا إلى الله” directs people to flee toward God; it gives another explicit movement of orientation toward Him, like the section’s final turn of desire.
terra: أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ imagines a demanded payment as debt that weighs the hearers down.

luna: In a passage about accounting and striving, the ayah states that no bearer of a burden bears another’s burden; it gives the boundary that the section’s contrast between Moses’ requested helper and God’s direct removal makes visible. | terra: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ is recalled as part of Moses’ and Abraham’s scrolls, reinforcing the boundary beside the section’s Moses–minister scene.

luna: After 53:38 states that one does not carry another’s burden, this ayah says a person has only what he strives for; its own contribution is the shift from load-bearing to personal effort, as in the section’s command after the burden is removed.

luna: Following 53:39’s statement of personal striving, this ayah says the striving will be seen; it adds the disclosure of directed effort to the section’s rise from hidden burden to publicly raised remembrance.
luna: After 53:39–40 describe effort and its being seen, this ayah says it will then be repaid fully; it completes the passage’s account of the consequence of one’s own labor.
terra: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ makes “to your Lord” the final endpoint, the destination implicit in the section’s commanded desire.
terra: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ directly fuses two of the section’s meetings: ease is made for remembrance.
terra: The repeated يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ makes ease and retained, voiced remembrance a recurring Quranic law rather than a single event.
terra: This third refrain again joins divinely made ease to dhikr, paralleling the section’s move from an eased load to elevated remembrance.
terra: The fourth يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ completes the repeated meeting of ease and remembrance.
terra: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ pairs raising with setting down, though the objects are sky and balance rather than name and burden.

luna: God says “سنفرغ لكم” to the two weighty beings; the source-section root f-r-gh is glossed as turning deliberately to a matter, and this distinct divine use likewise presents a directed engagement, though the wording and scene differ. | terra: سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ ٱلثَّقَلَانِ uses faragha for deliberate attention to an affair, the section’s secondary sense, but here as a warning from the divine speaker.
terra: Believers are asked whether the time has come for their hearts to become humble to God’s remembrance, joining an inwardly changed chest with active response to dhikr.
terra: God promises believers a light by which they may walk, closely corresponding to the section’s source gloss of a breast spread by divine light and then set in motion.
terra: يَرْفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ... دَرَجَٰتٍ uses divine raising for rank rather than physical height, one component of the section’s semantic meeting.
terra: Had the Quran descended on a mountain, it would be خَٰشِعًا مُّتَصَدِّعًا; a structure splits beneath revelatory weight where the section’s relieved back can stand.
terra: The donkey يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًا bears books as bodily cargo without receiving their guidance, joining the section’s back-load and forgotten-remembrance images.

luna: Believers are commanded to leave trade when called to Friday prayer and hasten to God’s remembrance; this is a concrete redirection from finished worldly work toward worship, preparing the action sequence in the next ayah. | terra: The call to remembrance commands فَٱسْعَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُوا۟ ٱلْبَيْعَ; ordinary work is emptied out for deliberate Lordward effort.

luna: After prayer is concluded, believers disperse to seek God’s bounty and remember Him much; this ayah contributes the specific post-task movement that parallels the section’s “when free, rise and turn desire to your Lord.” | terra: فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ sends worshippers back to work while retaining وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا, a complementary completion-and-new-task sequence.
terra: Within the divorce regulations, whoever remains mindful of God is promised a way out, introducing the concrete release and unexpected provision continued in 65:3.
terra: God provides from an unanticipated source, suffices the one who trusts Him, and has set a measure for everything; release, provision, and exact fitting meet.

luna: The waiting period for a pregnant woman ends when she delivers, and the ayah promises that God makes the affair easy for the God-conscious; it joins childbirth’s carried term to ease. | terra: Pregnant women’s term lasts أَن يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ, and the ayah concludes يَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِنْ أَمْرِهِۦ يُسْرًا; laying down a pregnancy and ease meet in one verse.

luna: This passage forbids harming a divorced mother to constrain her and speaks of nursing for payment and consultation; it gives the breastfeeding difficulty that the section names as another burden-bearing scene. | terra: حَتَّىٰ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ and وَإِن تَعَاسَرْتُمْ فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُۥٓ أُخْرَىٰ join delivery, nursing, and mutual difficulty in the section’s second birth scene.

luna: The source section sets 94’s “with hardship” beside this ayah’s “بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا” (ease after hardship); its own contribution is a real after-then-ease formulation that makes the section’s “with” relation distinctive. | terra: A person whose provision is restricted spends accordingly, then سَيَجْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا; its “after” sharpens surah 94’s stronger “with.”
terra: God makes the earth tractable, commands people to walk its pathways and eat His provision, then states that resurrection is to Him: work, provision, and return align.
terra: The one يَمْشِى مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ is opposed to one يَمْشِى سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ; bent and upright postures become moral directions.
terra: إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ is the closest verbal counterpart to the final command: desire is explicitly directed toward “our Lord.”
terra: People are called to prostrate on the Day but cannot, the bodily opposite of freely rising to obedient exertion; 68:43 explains their earlier refusal while able.
terra: They had been called to prostrate while sound, so their later inability exposes neglected capacity rather than a burden God first removed.
terra: The repeated question فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ again turns a financial liability into bodily heaviness, joining the debt and back-load images.
terra: The sky is split and becomes frail, contributing structural failure before 69:17 introduces the bearers above it.
terra: Angels stand at the sky’s edges and eight bear the Lord’s Throne above them, adding an exalted carried weight to 69:16’s broken structure.
terra: People rush from graves as though toward an erected marker; nasb becomes a target of frantic direction rather than upright work directed to the Lord.
terra: Whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord is driven into arduous punishment; rejected dhikr produces burden rather than the section’s release.
terra: The messenger says no one can protect him from God and he will find no مُلْتَحَدًا apart from Him, a direct semantic counterpart to لَا وَزَرَ and Lordward direction.
luna: The surah addresses a person wrapped in a cloak before commanding him to rise; this supplies a garment scene beside the section’s dictionary image of spreading a garment to carry a load.
luna: The wrapped person is commanded to stand at night in prayer; this is a concrete stand-and-work command alongside the section’s instruction to rise after the burden is taken away.

luna: After the night-standing command, God says a weighty word will be cast upon the Prophet; this contributes the heavy task that gives purpose to the work in the surrounding passage. | terra: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِى عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا presents revelation to the same prophetic addressee as a weighty word, the demanding counterpart to removal of his burden.

luna: The Prophet is told to remember his Lord’s name and devote himself wholly to Him; this joins the section’s raised-name motif to its final deliberate turn toward God. | terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا joins name-remembrance with deliberate, exclusive direction toward the Lord.
luna: The next instruction identifies God as Lord of east and west and commands taking Him as trustee; it contributes the explicit Lordward dependence that complements the section’s final direction.
luna: The Prophet is told to be patient with what people say and to leave them graciously; this adds patient work under opposition to the surrounding command to stand and take God as trustee.
terra: God knows the community’s sickness, travel, and struggle, so He repeatedly commands reciting what is easy and continues with prayer, giving, and forgiveness.
luna: The surah addresses the person wrapped in a cloak; this provides the garment context for its next command to rise, recalling the source section’s garment-and-standing images.

luna: The wrapped person is commanded to rise and warn; this is a direct command to move from being covered to purposeful work, like the section’s released person who stands. | terra: “Arise and warn” makes the prophetic addressee’s upright posture the beginning of a new commanded task.
luna: After the command to rise and warn, this ayah commands magnifying the Lord; it supplies the Godward purpose of the work.
luna: After describing the warning mission, this ayah commands patience for the Lord; it links strenuous work to its Lordward orientation.
terra: أَيْنَ ٱلْمَفَرُّ voices the fleeing human’s search; its own contribution is the question that “no refuge” answers in 75:11.

luna: The source section explicitly gives the secondary gloss of w-z-r as “shelter”; 75:11 says “لَا وَزَرَ,” no refuge, carrying that sense into the Judgment scene and clarifying why the section ends by turning to God. | terra: كَلَّا لَا وَزَرَ uses the section’s secondary sense of wazar, “refuge,” and denies every shelter before the destination named in 75:12.

luna: 75:11 denies refuge and 75:12 supplies “إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ”; the latter’s own contribution is the turn toward the Lord, matching the section’s final words and identifying the destination after refuge fails. | terra: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ completes “no refuge” with the same إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ direction that closes surah 94.
terra: “You love the immediate” identifies the desire that competes with Lordward orientation in the same surah that later denies refuge and names the Lord as destination.
terra: “You leave the Hereafter” contributes the abandoned endpoint paired with love of the immediate in 75:20.
terra: They love the immediate life and leave behind them a heavy day, joining worldly desire, what is cast behind, and an unescaped weight in one reversal.
terra: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّىٰهَا depicts a built canopy raised and made proportionate; 79:30 supplies the complementary spreading of earth.
terra: وَٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَىٰهَا contributes the spread ground beneath 79:28’s raised heaven, echoing the section’s building-and-expansion cluster.
luna: The one who transgressed and “آثر الحياة الدنيا” preferred worldly life; this is a direct opposite to the section’s final Godward desire.

luna: 79:37 names preference for worldly life, and this ayah says Hell is its shelter; its own contribution is the destination that makes the preference a consequential reversal of the section’s turning to God. | terra: Preferring the worldly life names the competing orientation for the section’s deliberately Lordward desire; 79:40 supplies the opposite stance.

luna: This ayah describes one who fears standing before his Lord and restrains the self from desire; it directly joins standing, the Lord, and renouncing a competing desire. | terra: Fearing the standing before one’s Lord and restraining the self from desire reverses worldly preference by giving desire a Lord-conscious boundary.
luna: After 79:40 describes restraint out of fear of the Lord, this ayah says the Garden is the shelter; its own contribution is the outcome of that Godward orientation.
terra: After human formation and measuring, ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ makes the birth-path easy, a concise nonlexical counterpart to the section’s childbirth-ease meeting.
terra: The day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds makes uprightness explicitly a posture of final Lordward encounter.

luna: The human is “كادح إلى ربك كدحا,” laboring toward the Lord and meeting Him; this directly joins the section’s wearied, Godward effort to its final orientation toward God. | terra: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا names the section’s final posture exactly in other words: strenuous work whose direction is the Lord.
terra: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا supplies the easy outcome for the human whose labor is explicitly toward the Lord in 84:6.
terra: سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى commands a voiced divine name together with height, an inverse but related meeting of name, sound, and elevation.
terra: سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰ promises the prophetic addressee remembrance rather than what is lost behind the back; 87:8–9 continue with ease and reminding.
terra: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ turns divine action upon the addressee into a course of ease, between the promise not to forget and the command to remind.
terra: فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ makes the divinely eased recipient act, reproducing the section’s shift from receiving God’s acts to obeying a command.

luna: People are said to prefer the nearer life; this is the precise worldly preference that the section names as a possible direction for the opened chest. | terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا names the rival direction for the desire and effort ordered toward the Lord in the section.

luna: 87:16 supplies preference for nearer life, and this ayah says the Hereafter is better and more lasting; it contributes the boundary that supports the section’s final orientation to God. | terra: وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ gives the enduring object opposed to nearer life, following the same passage’s ease and command to remember.

luna: The faces described as “عاملة ناصبة” are laboring and exhausted, but the surrounding passage gives them a severe punishment; the shared source-section root n-ṣ-b marks a boundary that exertion alone does not establish the right Godward direction. | terra: عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ depicts laboring, exhausted people entering fire; its nasb is toil without the fruitful Lordward orientation of the section’s command.

luna: 88:3 supplies the weary labor, and this next ayah adds “تسقى من عين آنية,” a drink from a boiling spring; this row completes the punishment that contrasts with the section’s Lord-directed effort.
terra: فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَّرْفُوعَةٌ supplies a raised object; the cup “placed” in 88:14 completes the vertical verb-pair found in the section.
terra: وَأَكْوَابٌ مَّوْضُوعَةٌ supplies the placed object beside the raised couches, a concrete lexical miniature of load put down and mention raised.
terra: أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلْإِبِلِ introduces the camel whose back and saddle underlie the section’s caravan image; the next three ayat supply raising, erecting, and spreading.
terra: وَإِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ contributes the raised structure in the camel–mountain–earth sequence that mirrors the section’s construction verbs.
terra: وَإِلَى ٱلْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ uses the section’s dictionary sense of nasb exactly: mountains are lifted and set upright.
terra: وَإِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ completes the sequence with the earth spread flat, corresponding to the section’s repeated image of expansion.
terra: A person treats generous provision as proof that “my Lord has honored me”; the assumption wrongly collapses economic expansion into elevated rank.
terra: When provision is constrained, the person says “my Lord has humiliated me”; this mistaken equation clarifies that narrow provision is not itself lowered status.
terra: “Return to your Lord, well pleased and pleasing” makes the final Lordward turn an answer of the tranquil soul.
luna: This ayah describes the one who gives and is mindful of God; it begins the paired path in which giving and orientation lead toward ease.
luna: After 92:5 names giving and God-consciousness, this ayah adds affirming the best; its own contribution is the belief attached to the path toward ease.

luna: After the giving, mindfulness, and affirmation in 92:5–6, this ayah says God will ease that person toward ease; it makes the connection between conduct and ease explicit. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ makes a person’s giving and God-conscious response lead into divinely granted ease.
luna: This ayah begins the contrary path with the one who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient; it sets a specific worldly stance opposite to the section’s desire for the Lord.
luna: After 92:8 describes withholding and self-sufficiency, this ayah adds denial of the best; it supplies the rejection that leads toward the contrary outcome.

luna: Following the withholding and denial in 92:8–9, this ayah says God will ease that person toward hardship; it gives a direct reversal of the section’s ease and Godward direction. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ paradoxically “eases” the miser toward difficulty, showing that facilitation takes its value from the end toward which one turns.
luna: The righteous person gives wealth to purify himself; this concrete emptying of what one has contributes a material image of release before the section’s turn toward the Lord.
luna: After 92:18 describes giving, this ayah says it is not repayment for a favor received; its own contribution removes an earthly payback motive from the act.

luna: After 92:19 rules out repayment, this ayah says the giving seeks only the face of the Most High Lord; it directly specifies the Godward aim the section’s last ayah commands. | terra: إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ makes generous exertion an exclusive seeking of the Most High Lord’s face.
luna: Following the act and its aim in 92:18–20, this ayah promises that the giver will be satisfied; it completes the relation between directed effort and its outcome.
terra: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَـَٔاوَىٰ begins the same addressee’s catalogue of received divine acts, which later changes into commands.
terra: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلًّا فَهَدَىٰ continues God’s acts upon a receptive addressee before the surah’s closing imperatives.
terra: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ recalls God relieving the same addressee’s need; the later commands make received benefaction produce action.
terra: فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ is the first commanded action arising from the favors in 93:6–8, structurally parallel to surah 94’s turn.
terra: وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ continues the recipient’s new responsibility before the final command to voice the Lord’s favor.
terra: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ commands the recipient to voice his Lord’s favor, meeting elevated audible remembrance and the final turn to the benefactor.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ gives the same addressee and direction as the section’s close, now explicitly as return.
terra: فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَيْتِ directs the beneficiaries to their Lord; 106:4 names the hunger and fear He removed.
terra: ٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍ grounds the command to worship in burdens relieved by the benefactor.
terra: إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ is a divine “We” gift to the addressee; 108:2 then changes him from recipient to commanded actor, exactly the section’s structural turn.
terra: فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ answers divine giving with effort explicitly “for your Lord,” paralleling the relieved recipient’s Lord-directed action.
terra: After divine help and completed victory, فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ turns the addressee from recipient into an active worshipper of his Lord.
